Shettima gave the commendation on Thursday, November 26, 2026, while commissioning three major infrastructure projects executed by the Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, in Ekwulobia, Aguata Local Government Area.
The projects included the Ekwulobia Flyover Bridge, Tower of Light, shopping mall and ancillary structures. While commending Soludo for his administration’s urban renewal projects, the Vice-President singled out Otti for praise, noting that political affiliation should not determine the recognition of good governance. “Governor Alex Otti was elected on the platform of the Labour Party, but he is doing wonderfully well. We must give credit where it is due,” he said. Shettima also commended Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, for his performance, describing his Imo State counterpart as a great politician and builder of roads and people. He also praised Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, for his efforts to address the state’s longstanding water supply challenges. According to him, Mbah demonstrated foresight by securing a loan from Zenith Bank and importing water pipes even before his inauguration, a move he said was beginning to improve access to pipe-borne water in the state. The Vice-President urged the people of the South-East to participate actively in national politics, stressing that the region’s importance to Nigeria should not be limited by ethnic considerations. “Ndigbo are too important to Nigeria to be confined to a tribal cocoon,” he said. He described Soludo as a courageous leader with strong convictions, commending him and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) for aligning with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Shettima said the partnership was already producing results in Anambra, citing the commissioned projects as evidence of the state’s development efforts. He described Soludo as the best governor in Anambra’s contemporary history and expressed confidence that his political career would extend beyond the governorship. The Vice-President urged Anambra residents to support Soludo’s administration through prayers, ideas and payment of taxes and levies. “Every naira honestly paid in revenue contributes to the roads, hospitals, schools and other public infrastructure that improve your lives,” he said. He also urged residents to protect public infrastructure against vandalism, maintain clean streets and ensure that trading activities did not obstruct roads and the flyover. “These facilities belong to you, and their future is in your hands. Remember, a governor can build a bridge, but only the people can keep it standing,” he said. Earlier, Soludo said the projects were part of his administration’s commitment to transforming Anambra into a liveable and prosperous state where residents could enjoy better living conditions and pursue their economic activities. The commissioning ceremony attracted several prominent personalities, including businessman, Sir Emeka Offor; Cardinal Peter Okpaleke; Chairman of the Anambra State Traditional Rulers Council, Igwe Chidubem Iweka III; and former Ohanaeze Ndigbo National Vice-President, Ichie Damian Okeke-Ogene. Others included APGA National Chairman, Chief Sly Ezeokenwa; the party’s Anambra State Chairman, Chief Ifeatu Obi-Okoye; former Senator Uche Ekwunife; and APGA chieftains, Chief Ben Obi and Chief Titus.
